claims.text: A machine-learning potential can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties of high-entropy systems.
A machine-learning potential can maintain accuracy while reducing that computational cost.
The proposed method applies to elemental, binary, and multicomponent systems in both solid and fluid states near phase transitions.
A machine-learning potential can predict free energies and relevant entropy terms.
The proposed potential can efficiently predict free energies and entropy terms for high-entropy systems.
Efficient prediction by the machine-learning potential will reduce computational cost relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
Efficient prediction by the machine-learning potential will reduce computational cost relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will improve efficiency in predicting fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed method may improve accuracy for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The intended composition domain includes elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The intended temperature domain is the high-temperature range near phase transitions.
